name: Fare Drop Watch — Flight Price Alerts from Your Watchlist

parameters.content:
## Fare Drop Watch — get alerted only when a fare actually drops
### How it works
You keep a watchlist of flights in a Google Sheet: origin, destination, dates, and an optional target price. Every morning this workflow runs each watch through the **Flight Price Watch** actor on Apify in watch mode. The actor remembers the fares it has seen, so repeat checks return only what changed. When a fare drops — or hits your target — you get one Slack alert per drop with the old price, the new price, and the booking link, and the drop is written to the Alert Log tab so it is never sent twice. Checks that find no drop cost nothing and send nothing.
### Setup
You need an Apify account (connect it on the "Check fares on Apify" node), a Google Sheet with two tabs — **Watchlist** (headers: origin, destination, departureDate, returnDate, targetPrice, cabinClass, currency) and **Alert Log** (headers: flightKey, route, departureDate, airlines, previousPrice, newPrice, dropPercent, changeType, alertedAt, link) — and a Slack channel for the alerts. Dates use YYYY-MM-DD. Point both Sheets nodes at your spreadsheet and set your channel on the Slack node.
### Customization
Raise max_alerts_per_watch if you watch busy routes, run the schedule twice a day for fast-moving fares, or swap the Slack node for Telegram or email — the alert text is already built for you.

## ⚠️ First check = baseline only
The first time a watch runs, the Actor records today's fares as its baseline and returns no drops. Alerts start from the second check. That is the watch working as designed — not a failure.

## 1 · Watchlist & settings
The settings node holds the per-run limits. The workflow reads the Alert Log first (its memory of drops already sent), then the Watchlist — one row per flight you want watched.

## 2 · Check each watch
Watches run one at a time. For each row the Apify actor searches Google Flights in watch mode: the first check stores today's fares as the baseline; later checks return only drops, target hits, and a summary.

## 3 · Only genuine drops pass
Baseline rows, summaries and errors are filtered out here. What survives is a PRICE_DROP or TARGET_HIT that is not already in the Alert Log — everything else routes back to the loop quietly.

## 4 · Alert, then log
One Slack message per drop: route, dates, airline, old price → new price, and the Google Flights link. The drop is then appended to the Alert Log, which is what stops the same drop being alerted twice.

parameters.customBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ routes: [{ origin: $json.origin, destination: $json.destination, departureDate: $json.departureDate, ...($json.returnDate ? { returnDate: $json.returnDate } : {}) }], mode: 'watch', ...($json.targetPrice ? { targetPrice: Number($json.targetPrice) } : {}), ...($json.cabinClass ? { cabinClass: String($json.cabinClass).toLowerCase() } : {}), ...($json.currency ? { currency: String($json.currency).toUpperCase() } : {}), maxResultsPerRoute: Number($('Set your watch settings').first().json.max_results_per_route) || 20 }) }}
